acceptedAnswer.text: Deep tissue massage is a technique that targets deeper layers of muscles and connective tissues. It uses slow, firm pressure to release chronic tension and break up adhesions in the body.
Deep tissue massage can be intense, but it should never be intolerable. You may feel some discomfort during deeper work, but communication with your therapist ensures a safe and effective experience.

mainEntity.name: What are the benefits of deep tissue massage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Benefits of deep tissue massage may include reduced muscle soreness, improved range of motion, tension relief, better posture, and enhanced recovery after physical activity.

mainEntity.name: How is deep tissue different from Swedish massage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Swedish massage uses lighter pressure and long, flowing strokes to promote relaxation, while deep tissue massage applies slower, deeper pressure to target knots and chronic muscle issues.

mainEntity.name: How often should I get a deep tissue massage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most people benefit from deep tissue massage every 2 to 4 weeks, depending on stress levels, physical activity, and recovery needs. Athletes or those with chronic tension may come more often.
